title: Verifying the Fix and Documenting the Work

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Office room with a newly repaired LED fixture; tech and customer standing under it. Matthew in foreground, medium shot.
scenes.says: The job isn't over when the light comes on. Safety first: re-energizing has its own hazards, so follow the lockout release procedure, and make sure every cover is on and everyone's clear. Plan the finish before you start: time to run the fixture, your clamp meter, a camera, and a clean way to haul out old parts. It works isn't the finish line.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Tech operates the wall switch and walks under the occupancy sensor; lights respond. Presenter voice-over.
scenes.says: Step one, operate it the way the customer does: the wall switch, occupancy sensor, dimmer, time clock or building schedule. A fixture that lights when you jumper it at the junction box but not from the sensor isn't fixed.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Tech checks neighboring fixtures, then the panel: breaker on, door closed. Then a timer on screen.
scenes.on_screen: 2 Check neighbors  3 Run it long enough
scenes.says: Step two, check the whole circuit and the neighbors. Opening splices in shared boxes can disturb other circuits. Make sure the breaker you locked out is back on and the panel door's closed. Step three, run it long enough. For a cycling or thermal problem, run it past the point where it used to fail, often 15 to 30 minutes, longer for HID warm-up.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Close-up: qualified tech measures supply at the fixture input and uses a clamp meter on the circuit; readings written down.
scenes.on_screen: 4 Measure: H-N, H-G, N-G | Load current | Breaker holds
scenes.says: Step four, measure and record. Supply voltage hot to neutral, hot to ground, and neutral to ground at the fixture input. Load current with a clamp meter, as a baseline for next time. Breaker holds. And light output meets what the customer expects.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Above-ceiling shot: insulation pulled off a fixture top; tiles replaced, lens installed, old parts bagged.
scenes.on_screen: 5 Root cause?  6 Leave it clean and safe
scenes.says: Step five, ask: did I fix why it failed? If a driver cooked from heat, fix the heat or report it. Step six, leave it clean and safe. Covers and lenses on, labels applied, no debris, tiles back and undamaged, waste lamps and ballasts packed for disposal. Before re-energizing: tools out, guards on, everyone clear and notified, then remove your own lock. Never remove someone else's.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Tablet close-up: tech fills in the work order fields: location, complaint, verified symptom, readings, cause, repair, verification, follow-up, circuit, parts, photos.
scenes.on_screen: "Voltage good" is opinion. "276 V H-N" is data.
scenes.says: Documentation is part of the repair. Record location in the customer's language, the complaint, the verified symptom, tests and readings, cause, repair, verification, follow-up, the circuit and parts, plus before and after photos. Record readings with units. Voltage good is opinion. 276 volts hot to neutral is data. And note what you didn't fix, and why.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Supervisor at a desk with two printed sample work orders, one vague, one complete; Matthew narrates.
scenes.on_screen: "Fixed light" vs a complete work order
scenes.says: Here's a supervisor comparing two work orders. One says fixed light. That tells nobody anything. The other says: failed LED driver, housing very hot, insulation laid on the fixture, driver replaced, insulation removed, ran 20 minutes from switch and sensor, recommend checking the other fixtures in the room. That one lets the next tech start where you left off, and shows the customer the value.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Tech talks to the customer under the working fixture; customer signs the tablet.
scenes.on_screen: Found → did → show → recommend → explain → sign
scenes.says: Close with the customer. Tell them what you found and did, in plain language. Show them it works. Mention related problems or recommendations without overselling, and note them for your lead. Explain anything they might notice, like HID restrike delay, a new LED color, or a sensor timeout. Get a signature if the work order needs it.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.says: Verify it the customer's way, write it so the next tech can use it, and close the loop. Now read the lesson and take the quiz.

production_notes: Customer walk-through and supervisor review per the lesson's video suggestion. Use sanitized sample work orders (the lesson's example fields are fine; no real customer or building names). Energized readings by a qualified tech in PPE. Show the LOTO release order on screen if time allows.
